record.original_question: Draw a study of the recurrence quotients for other families of infinite word that sturmian words, such as words of complexity 2n + 1, or toinfinite words in general.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over a finite alphabet $A$. The factor complexity of $w$ is the function $p_w(n)$ counting the number of distinct factors (contiguous finite subwords) of $w$ of length $n$. The word $w$ is uniformly recurrent if for every $n$ there exists an integer $R_w(n)$ such that every factor of $w$ of length $R_w(n)$ contains every factor of $w$ of length $n$ as a factor; the smallest such integer defines the recurrence function $R_w(n)$. The recurrence quotient of $w$ is defined as
$$\rho(w) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{R_w(n)}{n}.$$

For Sturmian words (the aperiodic infinite words of factor complexity $p_w(n) = n + 1$), the recurrence quotient has been studied in detail and is closely related to the continued fraction expansion of the slope.

Carry out an analogous systematic study of the recurrence quotient $\rho(w)$ for other families of infinite words beyond Sturmian words. In particular:
(a) Determine $\rho(w)$, or its possible range of values, for infinite words of factor complexity $p_w(n) = 2n + 1$ (for instance Arnoux–Rauzy words on a three-letter alphabet, or more generally episturmian and ternary words of this complexity).
(b) More broadly, develop a theory of the recurrence quotient for arbitrary uniformly recurrent infinite words, identifying which values of $\rho(w)$ can be attained and how $\rho(w)$ relates to combinatorial parameters such as factor complexity, balance, and frequencies of letters.
artifact.status_search_result: Cassaigne and Chekhova explicitly computed the recurrence function for Arnoux–Rauzy sequences (which have factor complexity 2n+1), giving partial answers for that subfamily. However, a comprehensive theory of the recurrence quotient for all infinite words of complexity 2n+1 and for general (uniformly recurrent) infinite words has not been established, so the program described remains only partially addressed.

status_evidence.snippet: Computation of the recurrence function of Arnoux–Rauzy sequences, answering a question of Morse and Hedlund.
status_evidence.claim: The recurrence function has been computed for the Arnoux–Rauzy family (complexity 2n+1), giving partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Recurrence in infinite words (Cassaigne)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on recurrence functions and recurrence quotients of infinite words, mainly focusing on Sturmian and Arnoux–Rauzy cases.
status_evidence.claim: General theory of the recurrence quotient beyond Sturmian/Arnoux–Rauzy words remains incomplete.
